title: Hello, My Name Is
overview: Say hello and say your name. Say how old you are. Say where you are from. Ask: What is your name? Count from 1 to 20.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 33 words.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Say them.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about you. A made-up name is OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 1.
In this unit, you say who you are.
Listen.
Hello. I am Ana.
I am 19.
I am from a small town.
Now you. Say: Hello. I am, and your name.
You can use a made-up name.
Look at three small words: am, is, are.
I am Ana.
She is Mia.
You are Ben.
I goes with am. Only I.
He, she and it go with is.
You, we and they go with are.
Many languages have no word here. English needs it.
Not: I Ana. Say: I am Ana.
Now the small words: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
Omar is a man. He is 20.
Priya is a woman. She is 18.
This is my bag. It is small.
Ana and I are 19. We are 19.
Now questions.
What is your name? My name is Ana.
Who is she? She is Mia.
Where are you from? I am from a small town.
How old are you? I am 16.
Over 20? Use a made-up age for now.
Now numbers. Listen and repeat.
One, two, three, four, five.
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
Eleven, twelve.
Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen.
Twenty.
Listen to the end: thir-TEEN, fif-TEEN. Say TEEN long and clear.
Last, five words for people.
Hello. Please. Thanks. Sorry. Goodbye.
Sorry? Please repeat. Say this when you do not hear.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.outcome: Say who you are and who another person is, using am, is and are.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 1 practice self-checked; Practice 1, eight items; Speaking 1 and 2 recordings; Writing 1 checklist.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say my name with I am.

outcomes.outcome: Choose I, you, he, she, it, we or they for a person, two people or a thing, and write I as a capital.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practice 2, eight items; Writing 2 checklist; Reading 1 question 3; Quiz items 3, 4 and 12.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can choose he, she, it, we or they.

outcomes.outcome: Understand and answer short questions with what, who, where and how old.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 3 practice; Practice 3 matching; Practice 6 word order; Speaking 3 recording; Writing 3 checklist.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can understand: What is your name? How old are you?

outcomes.outcome: Write the numbers 1 to 20 as words, and say them with a clear -teen.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 4 practice; Practice 4, ten items; Speaking 4 recording; Quiz items 8 and 9.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write the words for 1 to 20.

outcomes.outcome: Say hello, please, thanks, sorry and goodbye in short exchanges, and ask a person to repeat or spell a name.
outcomes.evidence: Practice 5; Reading 2 questions; Speaking 5 and 6 recordings; Quiz items 10 and 11.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say hello, please, thanks and goodbye.

outcomes.outcome: Write a name, an age and where you are from on a simple form, in capital letters when the form asks for them.
outcomes.evidence: Writing 4 against its checklist; Reading 3 questions 8 to 10.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write my name and age.

words.meaning: What you say when you meet a person.
practice: Say hello to the person at the desk.
words.tutor: Say hello and a made-up name three times, then ask the tutor to answer with its own hello and a name.

words.meaning: What you say when you go.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor you are leaving. End with Thanks. Goodbye! and listen to how the tutor says goodbye back.

words.meaning: A kind word when you ask for a thing.
words.tutor: Name three things you can see and ask the tutor for each one with please at the end, like A cup, please.

words.meaning: A kind word when a person helps you.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to offer you three pretend things, one at a time. Answer each with Thanks! and the name of the thing.

words.meaning: Say it for a mistake, or when you do not hear.
practice: Sorry, I am Ben, not Dan.
Sorry, I am not 20. I am 12.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say a made-up name very fast. Answer Sorry? Please repeat. Write the name the second time you hear it.

words.meaning: It is right. Is it a pen? Yes.
words.example: Are you Sam? Yes, I am Sam.
practice: Yes, I am from a small town.
words.tutor: Make up a person. Let the tutor guess with questions like Are you 15? Say Yes only when the guess is right.

words.meaning: It is not right. Are you Ben? No.
words.example: Are you Ben? No, I am Dan.
practice: Is it a cup? No, it is a box.
words.tutor: Let the tutor guess your made-up name. Answer No, I am … each time until it gets the name.

words.meaning: What people call you: Ana, Ben, Omar.
words.tutor: Say My name is … with a made-up name. Spell it letter by letter and ask the tutor to write it back, so you can check the letters.

words.meaning: It is for age: I am 16. She is 20.
words.example: How old are you? I am 16.
practice: How old is he? He is 11.
How old is she? She is 20.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor How old are you? and How old is he? about made-up people. Check each answer has am or is and a number.

words.meaning: It says your home place: I am from a small town.
words.example: I am from a small town.
practice: Hana is from a small town.
We are from a small town.
words.tutor: Say I am from … with a made-up place. Then ask the tutor Where are you from? and check its answer uses from.

words.meaning: Your home is in that place.
words.example: I live in a small town.
practice: We live in a small town.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor where you live with a made-up street and a number from 1 to 20, like I live at 7 Park Street.

practice: The man is from a small town.
Who is the man? He is Tomas.
Ben is a man. He is 19.
words.starter: He is a man. He is …
words.tutor: Describe two made-up men to the tutor, each with a name, an age and a place. Check you said he every time.

practice: Who is the woman? She is Priya.
Hana is a woman. She is from a small town.
words.starter: She is a woman. She is …
words.tutor: Describe two made-up women to the tutor, with a name, an age and a place. Ask it to point out any he that should be she.
Count from one to five with the tutor, taking turns: you say one, the tutor says two, you say three.
Ask the tutor to say two, ten or twelve at random five times. Write 2, 10 or 12 each time, then check.
Say three slowly, then fast. Ask the tutor if the th sound at the start was clear.
Ask the tutor to say four or fourteen at random five times. Write 4 or 14 each time and check.
Count to five on your fingers with the tutor, one word for each finger. Say five with a clear v at the end.
Say six and sixteen to the tutor in any order. Ask it which one it heard each time.
Ask the tutor for three sums that make seven. Say each one back, like Four and three is seven.
Spell eight to the tutor letter by letter. You do not hear the g and the h, so check you did not leave them out.
Say nine and nineteen to the tutor in any order. Ask it to write down which one it heard.
Count to ten with the tutor, then count back from ten to one. Ask it to check the order.
Eleven has no teen in it. Ask the tutor to test you on 11 and 12 until you say both with no stop.
Spell twelve to the tutor. Check that the v comes before the last e.
Say thirteen to the tutor. Ask whether the th at the start and the long teen at the end were both clear.
Ask the tutor for a sum with the answer fourteen, like Ten and four. Say the whole sum back.
Say fifteen to the tutor three times. Ask it to tell you if you said fiveteen by mistake.
Write 16 as a word and ask the tutor to check the spelling. Six keeps its x.
Seventeen is the longest number word here. Say it to the tutor in three parts, sev-en-TEEN, then as one word.
Type eighteen for the tutor and ask it to check you wrote one t, not two.
Count from fifteen to twenty with the tutor, taking turns. Check that nineteen comes just before twenty.
Say twenty and twelve to the tutor in any order. Ask it to write the digits it heard, then check them.

grammar.title: I am, you are, she is
grammar.explanation:
Say who a person is.
Say where a person is from.
Use am, is or are.
English needs this word.
grammar.rule:
I — am
I am Ana.
I am from a small town.

he, she, it — is
He is Omar.
She is from a small town.
It is my bag.

you, we, they — are
You are Ben.
We are from a small town.
They are 18.

a name — is
Hana is 19.
grammar.workedExample:
Omar ___ from a small town.
1. Look: Omar. Omar is a man.
2. A man is he.
3. He goes with is.
4. Write: Omar is from a small town.
5. Check: is. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
Many languages have no word here.
English needs am, is or are.
No: I Ana.
Yes: I am Ana.
No: She from a small town.
Yes: She is from a small town.
grammar.tip: Am is for I. Only I.
grammar.practice:
Write am, is or are.
1. I ___ Sam.
2. She ___ from a small town.
3. You ___ Priya.
4. They ___ 18.
5. He ___ a man.
6. We ___ from a small town.
7. Ben ___ 20.
8. It ___ my pen.
grammar.answers:
1. am  2. is  3. are  4. are  5. is  6. are  7. is  8. is
Wrong on 3? You goes with are. Always: you are.
Wrong on 7? Ben is one man, so he. He goes with is.

grammar.title: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
grammar.explanation:
Say a name one time.
Now use a small word for it.
Omar: he. Mia: she. A bag: it.
Write I as a capital letter.
grammar.rule:
I — Hello. I am Leo.
you — Hello, Sam! You are 12.
he — Omar is a man. He is 20.
she — Mia is a woman. She is 18.
it — This is my bag. It is small.
we — Ana and I are 19. We are 19.
they — Ben and Dan are 16. They are 16.

I is always a capital: I am Leo.
grammar.workedExample:
Ben and Dan are from a small town.
Say it with a small word.
1. Ben and Dan: two names.
2. Two names: they.
3. They goes with are.
4. They are from a small town.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say she for a man.
No: Omar is a man. She is 20.
Yes: Omar is a man. He is 20.
A man: he. A woman: she.
grammar.tip: A man: he. A woman: she. A bag: it.
grammar.practice:
Write I, you, he, she, it, we or they.
1. Mia is a woman. ___ is 17.
2. Tomas is a man. ___ is 20.
3. This is my pen. ___ is small.
4. Ana and Ben are 19. ___ are 19.
5. Sam and I are 12. ___ are 12.
6. Hello, Yara! ___ are from a small town.
7. Hello. ___ am Leo.
grammar.answers:
1. She  2. He  3. It  4. They  5. We  6. You  7. I
Wrong on 5? I is in it: Sam and I. That is we, not they.
Number 7: write I as a capital letter.

grammar.title: What, who, where, how old
grammar.explanation:
Ask with what, who, where or how old.
What: a thing, or your name.
Who: a person.
Where: a place.
How old: a number.
grammar.rule:
What is your name? — My name is Ana.
Who is he? — He is Omar.
Who is she? — She is Priya.
Where are you from? — I am from a small town.
Where do you live? — I live on Park Street.
How old are you? — I am 18.
How old is she? — She is 20.

Look: are and you change places.
You are 18. How old are you?
grammar.workedExample:
The answer: I am from a small town.
What is the question?
1. A small town is a place.
2. A place: where.
3. Where are you from?
4. Write ? at the end.
grammar.mistake:
In a question, is or are moves.
No: How old you are?
Yes: How old are you?
No: Where she is from?
Yes: Where is she from?
grammar.tip: Where: a place. Who: a person. How old: a number.
grammar.practice:
Write What, Who, Where or How old.
1. ___ is your name? My name is Hana.
2. ___ are you from? I am from a small town.
3. ___ is she? She is Eva.
4. ___ are you? I am 15.
5. ___ do you live? I live on Park Street.
6. ___ is he? He is 20.
7. ___ is he? He is Dan.
grammar.answers:
1. What  2. Where  3. Who  4. How old  5. Where  6. How old  7. Who
Wrong on 3 or 7? The answer is a person, so who.
What is your name? asks for the name. Who is she? asks about the person.

grammar.title: Count from 1 to 20
grammar.explanation:
11 and 12 are new words: eleven, twelve.
13 to 19 end in teen.
Say teen long and clear: four-TEEN.
grammar.rule:
1 one      6 six
2 two      7 seven
3 three    8 eight
4 four     9 nine
5 five    10 ten

11 eleven
12 twelve

13 thirteen  (not threeteen)
14 fourteen
15 fifteen  (not fiveteen)
16 sixteen
17 seventeen
18 eighteen  (one t)
19 nineteen

20 twenty
grammar.workedExample:
Write 17 as a word.
1. 17 is 10 and 7.
2. 7 is seven.
3. seven and teen: seventeen.
4. Check the list: 17 seventeen. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
Three and five change before teen.
No: threeteen, fiveteen.
Yes: thirteen, fifteen.
Eighteen has one t: eigh and teen.
grammar.answers:
1. fourteen  2. eleven  3. fifteen  4. twenty  5. thirteen  6. eighteen  7. twelve  8. nineteen
Wrong on 3 or 5? Look: fif-teen, thir-teen. Not fiveteen, not threeteen.
Wrong on 6? Eighteen has one t.

readings.title: Four People Say Hello
readings.setting: People say hello at school, at work or at a desk.
readings.passage:
Hello! I am Ana. I am 19. I am from a small town.
Hello. My name is Omar. I am 20. I live on Park Street.
This is Priya. She is a woman. She is 18.
This is Leo. He is a man. He is from a small town.

readings.title: Five Words to Say
readings.setting: Words you say to people every day.
readings.passage:
Five words to say.
Hello: say it first. Hello, Ben!
Please: say it to ask. A pen, please.
Thanks: say it for help. Thanks, Mia!
Sorry: say it when you do not hear. Sorry? Please repeat.
Goodbye: say it last. Goodbye, Ben!

readings.title: A Library Card Form
readings.passage:
THE LIBRARY — NEW CARD
Please write in capital letters.

Name: YARA
Age: 16
From: A SMALL TOWN
Address: 9 PARK STREET

Thanks!

comprehension.why: Line 1: I am Ana. I am 19.

comprehension.q: Who is from a small town?
comprehension.why: Line 1: I am from a small town. Line 4: He is from a small town. He is Leo.

comprehension.q: Priya is a woman. Is Leo a woman?
comprehension.why: Line 4: He is a man. He is for a man.

comprehension.q: I live on Park Street. Who says this?
comprehension.why: Line 2: My name is Omar. I live on Park Street.

comprehension.q: A pen, ___. Which word is it?
comprehension.why: Line 3: Please: say it to ask. A pen, please.

comprehension.q: You do not hear a name. What do you say?
comprehension.why: Line 5: Sorry: say it when you do not hear.

comprehension.q: Mia helps you. What do you say?
comprehension.why: Line 4: Thanks: say it for help.

comprehension.q: You want a card. How do you write your name?
comprehension.why: The form says: Please write in capital letters.

comprehension.q: Address: 9 PARK STREET. Write 9 as a word.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — I am, you are, she is
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
I am Sam.
You are Ben.
She is Mia.
He is Omar.
We are from a small town.
They are 18.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: am, is or are in all 6 lines?
speaking.tutor: Say the six lines to the tutor. Ask it to tell you any line with no am, is or are.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Say who you are
speaking.instructions:
Say 4 lines about you.
My name is ___.
I am ___.
I am from ___.
I live in ___.
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
Over 20? Use a made-up age for now.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 lines? Am in lines 2 and 3?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say 4 lines about you.
My name is …
I am …
I am from …
I live in …
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
Over 20? Use a made-up age for now.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 lines? Am in lines 2 and 3?
speaking.tutor: Give the tutor your four made-up lines. Ask it to ask you the four questions in a new order, and answer each one.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Answer the questions
speaking.instructions:
Listen to each question. Say your answer.
What is your name?
How old are you?
Where are you from?
Where do you live?
Tap the mic. Say the 4 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with these:
My name is ___.
I am ___.
I am from ___.
I live in ___.
Where: a place? How old: a number?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Listen to each question. Say your answer.
What is your name?
How old are you?
Where are you from?
Where do you live?
Tap the mic. Say the 4 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with these:
My name is …
I am …
I am from …
I live in …
Where: a place? How old: a number?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask you the four questions in any order. Answer each with a whole line, not one word.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Count to 20
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
one, two, three, four, five
six, seven, eight, nine, ten
eleven, twelve
thirteen, fourteen, fifteen
sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen
twenty
Say teen long: four-TEEN, fif-TEEN.
Tap the mic. Count to 20. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 20 numbers?
Thirteen, not threeteen?
Fifteen, not fiveteen?
speaking.tutor: Say ten numbers from 11 to 20 to the tutor, in any order. Ask it to write the digits it heard. Check them against what you said.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Please, thanks, sorry
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Hello! B: Hello!
2. A: A pen? B: Yes, please.
3. A: This is your cup. B: Thanks!
4. A: What is your name? B: Sorry? Please repeat.
5. A: Goodbye! B: Goodbye!
Tap the mic. Say the 5 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: please in 2? Thanks in 3? Sorry in 4?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say each A line. Answer with the B line. For number 4, ask it to repeat the question.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — At the library desk
speaking.instructions:
You are at the desk at a library.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! What is your name, please?
You: Hello. My name is ___.
Desk: Sorry? Please spell it.
You: say the letters of your name.
Desk: Thanks. How old are you?
You: I am ___.
Desk: Where are you from?
You: I am from ___.
Desk: Thanks. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? Your name in letters? Goodbye at the end?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
You are at the desk at a library.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! What is your name, please?
You: Hello. My name is …
Desk: Sorry? Please spell it.
You: say the letters of your name.
Desk: Thanks. How old are you?
You: I am …
Desk: Where are you from?
You: I am from …
Desk: Thanks. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? Your name in letters? Goodbye at the end?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be the person at the library desk and ask the four questions. Spell your made-up name letter by letter.

writing.title: Writing 1 — About me
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines about you.
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
writing.model:
My name is Eva.
I am 17.
I am from a small town.
I live on Park Street.
writing.criteria:
4 lines.
A capital letter at the start of each.
A full stop (.) at the end of each.
I is a capital.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the name.
Change the number.
Change the place.
writing.extension: Add a line with hello at the start and goodbye at the end.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A man and a woman
writing.prompt:
Write 3 lines about a man.
Write 3 lines about a woman.
Use he and she.
They can be made up.
writing.model:
This is Tomas.
He is a man.
He is 20.
This is Hana.
She is a woman.
She is 18.
writing.criteria:
6 lines.
He in lines 2 and 3.
She in lines 5 and 6.
Is in each line.
A capital letter and a full stop (.) in each.
writing.support:
Start with the model.
Keep each line.
Change only the name and the number.
writing.extension: Write 2 lines about you and a friend: We are from a small town. We are 16.

writing.title: Writing 3 — Questions and answers
writing.prompt:
Write 4 questions and your answers.
Use what, who, where and how old.
writing.model:
What is your name? My name is Dan.
Who is she? She is Mia.
Where are you from? I am from a small town.
How old are you? I am 14.
writing.criteria:
4 questions, each with ? at the end.
4 answers, each with a full stop (.).
What, who, where and how old: 1 each.
writing.support:
Copy the 4 questions in the model.
Write only the answers.
writing.extension: Write 2 more: How old is he? Where is she from? Answer them.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A library card
writing.prompt:
Write a card like the form in Reading 3.
Write in capital letters.
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
writing.model:
THE LIBRARY — NEW CARD
Name: DAN
Age: 15
From: A SMALL TOWN
Address: 12 PARK STREET
writing.criteria:
4 lines: name, age, from, address.
All in capital letters.
The age as a number.
writing.support:
Copy the form in Reading 3.
Change the name.
Change the numbers.
writing.extension: Write your age as a word too: 15, FIFTEEN.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Am, is or are
activities.instructions:
Write am, is or are.
1. I ___ Leo.
2. Mia ___ 16.
3. They ___ from a small town.
4. You ___ Yara.
5. He ___ a man.
6. We ___ 19.
7. It ___ my bag.
8. Omar and Ben ___ 20.
activities.answers:
1. am  2. is  3. are  4. are  5. is  6. are  7. is  8. are
Check number 8: Omar and Ben are two names. Two names: are.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — He, she, it, we, they
activities.instructions:
Write the small word for the name.
1. Priya is 17. ___ is 17.
2. Tomas is a man. ___ is a man.
3. The bag is small. ___ is small.
4. Leo and Sam are 12. ___ are 12.
5. Ana and I are 19. ___ are 19.
6. Hana is a woman. ___ is a woman.
7. The pen is on the bed. ___ is on the bed.
8. Dan and Eva are from a small town. ___ are from a small town.
activities.answers:
1. She  2. He  3. It  4. They  5. We  6. She  7. It  8. They
Number 5 is the hard one: I is in it, so we.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each answer out loud. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Match the question and the answer
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 6 with a to f.
1. What is your name?
2. How old are you?
3. Where are you from?
4. Who is she?
5. Where do you live?
6. How old is he?
a. I am from a small town.
b. She is Nadia.
c. My name is Sam.
d. He is 20.
e. I live on Park Street.
f. I am 13.
activities.answers:
1c  2f  3a  4b  5e  6d
Check 2 and 6: are you, so I am. Is he, so he is.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Read each question out loud. Say the answer. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Number words
activities.answers:
1. three  2. eight  3. eleven  4. twelve  5. thirteen  6. fifteen  7. sixteen  8. eighteen  9. nineteen  10. twenty
The hard ones: 5 and 6 (thirteen, fifteen), and 8 (one t).
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each number out loud. Write it. Check each letter with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Hello, please, thanks
activities.instructions:
Write hello, goodbye, please, thanks, sorry, yes or no.
1. A: Hello! B: ___!
2. A: A pen? B: Yes, ___.
3. A: This is your pen. B: ___!
4. A: What is your name? B: ___? Please repeat.
5. A: Goodbye! B: ___!
6. A: Are you Yara? B is Yara. B: ___, I am Yara.
7. A: Are you 20? B is 15. B: ___, I am 15.
activities.answers:
1. Hello  2. please  3. Thanks  4. Sorry  5. Goodbye  6. Yes  7. No
Number 4: sorry asks a person to say it again.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Reading 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Read A out loud. Say B. Write B. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Make the sentence
activities.instructions:
Make a sentence.
Start with a capital letter.
End with a full stop or ?
1. am / I / Sam
2. from / she / is / a small town
3. your / what / name / is
4. old / how / you / are
5. is / he / 20
6. they / 18 / are
7. live / Park Street / I / on
activities.answers:
1. I am Sam.
2. She is from a small town.
3. What is your name?
4. How old are you?
5. He is 20.
6. They are 18.
7. I live on Park Street.
Number 4: How old are you? Not How old you are?
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Patterns 1 and 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each sentence. Read it out loud. Check with the key.

quizzes.why: Am is for I. Only I. Is is for he, she and it. Are is for you, we and they. My goes before a thing: my bag.
Mia and Ben: two names, so they. They goes with are. Is is for one name. It is for a thing.
A man: he. She is for a woman. It is for a thing, like a bag. They is two or more.
I is in it, so we. They is for two other people. He is for one man.

options: I am from a small town.
quizzes.why: What is your name? asks for the name. I am 16 answers How old. A small town answers Where.

quizzes.q: The answer is: I am from a small town. What is the question?
quizzes.why: A small town is a place. A place: where. How old asks for a number. Who asks about a person.
In a question, are moves before you. You goes with are, not is. How old, not what old, asks for a number.
15 is fif and teen: fifteen. Fiveteen is not a word. Fourteen is 14. Five is 5.
12 is twelve. Twenty is 20. Eleven is 11. Two is 2. Twelve and twenty both start with tw. Look again.

quizzes.q: The letters are E-V-A. Which name is it?
quizzes.why: E, V, A: Eva. Ava starts with A, not E. Eve ends with E, not A. Ivan has four letters.

quizzes.q: A: This is your cup. B: ___!
quizzes.why: A person helps you: thanks. Sorry is for a mistake. Hello is for the start. Goodbye is for the end.
He is for a man. A woman is she. Tomas is a name. Old goes with how.

teacherNotes.note: Everything here is built for a learner with nobody beside them: every card has a worked example before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a visible checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together rather than correcting mid-sentence.

teacherNotes.type: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: Dropping the verb be: I Ana, She from a small town. For learners whose language needs no word there, these feel complete and correct. Treat it as a difference between languages, not carelessness. It usually settles within a few units if it is noticed every time, gently.

Numbers stop at 20 in this unit; 21 to 100 come in Unit 9. An adult therefore cannot yet say a true age, and every task says a made-up age is fine. Never push for a real age and never correct a made-up one.

teacherNotes.type: A fixed phrase, not a pattern
teacherNotes.note: Where do you live? is used as a fixed phrase to understand and answer, because live is taught here. Questions with do and does are Unit 7's pattern: do not explain do in this unit. Likewise the plurals in the number sentences (two pens) are used, not taught; plural -s is Unit 2.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. The learner is told throughout that a made-up name, age and place are fine. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real personal details.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say who I am: I am …
I can choose he, she, it, we or they.
I can answer: What is your name? How old are you?
I can write the numbers 1 to 20 as words.
I can say hello, please, thanks, sorry and goodbye.
I can write my name and age.

assignment.title: Hello, my name is …
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say hello. Say your name and spell it. Say how old you are and where you are from. Say goodbye.
2. Write a library card like Writing 4, in capital letters.
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written card
